prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the bright nearby ground and person from the darker shrubs, cliffs, sky, and pickup truck: the person is roughly 2–4 m in front of the camera wearer, the fabric bundle is about 2–4 m away and low on the ground, and the truck is farther back at roughly 6–10 m. Across the five frames, the person shifts from near the centre-right to the left, returns near centre, then appears on the right and becomes larger in the last frame, indicating changing camera orientation and a final approach to roughly 1–2 m. The person and bundle are usually separated by about 1–3 m, while neither appears consistently within the camera wearer's arm's reach until the person may be close to that boundary in frame 5. Depth makes foreground/background separation and the person's changing distance clearer than RGB, but distances are only rough: the washed-out foreground, merged shrubs and rocks, blurred final frame, and nearly uniform brightness across each person make fine geometry and occlusion ordering unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates a person in each frame, generally 2–4 m ahead and moving from centre-right to centre-left, centre, centre-right, and finally the right side close to the camera; it also separates several nearby ground objects from the black background. It shows object extents and partial overlaps clearly—for example, the person's arm projects rightward in frames 1–2, some objects lie immediately to that side or below it, and small detections near the far left or frame edges are partly out of view. Relative distances cannot be recovered directly from this map, but RGB and mask size suggest the ground bundle is about 2–4 m away, the truck about 6–10 m away, and the final person about 1–2 m away; objects beside the person appear within roughly an arm's length of that person in frames 1–2. Reliability is poor for object identity: masks labelled cow, car, umbrella, kite, and suitcase often conflict with the RGB, several visible scene elements are missing, adjacent items merge, and the final frame omits most objects besides the person.
descriptions.pose: The pose map extracts one main upright body in frames 1, 2, and 5, placing it centre-left, near centre, and right respectively; the changing skeleton size supports a distance of roughly 2–4 m initially and about 1–2 m in the last frame. In frame 1 the torso is mostly side-on with one arm extended toward image right, while frame 2 is more front-facing or oblique and frame 5 is again largely side-on; head keypoints alone do not reliably establish whether the person is looking directly at the camera wearer. The extended arm in frame 1 reaches toward an object or region beside the person, apparently within that person's arm's reach, but the map shows no camera-wearer skeleton and therefore cannot establish what is within the wearer's reach. Pose clarifies limb orientation against dark clothing better than RGB, but it is unreliable across the sequence: frame 3 has only a few disconnected points, frame 4 has no detected pose, hands are largely absent, and missing or displaced joints prevent dependable occlusion, above/below, and facing estimates.
